title: Design Generative AI for Practitioners: Exploring Interaction Approaches Aligned with Creative Practice
venue: Bidirectional Human-AI Alignment Workshop of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
extended_summary:
This position paper argues that current generative AI interaction paradigms often misalign with professional design practice because they overemphasize prompts or whole-image manipulation while design work is iterative, reflective, and distributed across multiple representations. The paper asks how GenAI interaction can better support creative practitioners’ intent, workflow, and control across the full arc of design activity.

To address this, the authors synthesize and present three interaction approaches—DesignPrompt, FusAIn, and DesignTrace—that shift alignment across different stages of the process: decomposing intent into multimodal scaffolds, directly manipulating visual prompts via pen-like tools, and tracking iterative design workflows through structured traces. These are conceptual examples drawn from prior systems and related HCI work rather than a new empirical study in K-12 science education.

The paper’s discussion centers on professional designers, not students or classrooms, and frames AI as a partner whose initiative should shift between proactive and reactive roles depending on the creative stage and user need. Its main conclusion is that alignment is not a static property of a single prompt or output, but a dynamic, multi-stage negotiation supported by heterogeneous interaction structures.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper/theoretical workshop-style contribution, not an empirical K-12 causal comparison study. It does not report a study design, sample, outcomes, or effect estimates relevant to educational impact assessment.
impact_tier_rationale: No student learning or K-12 implementation outcomes are reported. The paper discusses design principles for GenAI in professional design practice, so there is no evidence of impact on educational outcomes.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual design of generative AI interaction paradigms for professional creative practice, including multimodal intent scaffolds, direct visual prompt manipulation, and trackable iterative workflows
